name: Hive
summary: Project management and team collaboration in one workspace. Plan projects, assign tasks and centralize communication so work keeps moving.
best_for: project teams that want flexible PM (Gantt, Kanban, forms, chat) and only pay for the modules they actually use
skip_if: you need most of the add-ons anyway (all-inclusive tools price better), or your org demands one standardized suite
honest_knock: The seat price is honest bait, the add-on grid is the business model: switch on three add-ons and your $12 seat becomes $27 — a la carte flexibility that punishes teams who need the full toolkit. List your must-have modules first and compare the DRESSED price against all-inclusive rivals; for teams needing only core PM, though, Hive is genuinely cheap and pleasant. In our test on 21 October 2026 two defaults stood out: onboarding lets everyone on your email domain join the workspace automatically unless you untick it, and completed tasks disappear from the List view behind a filter.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month, yearly billing
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-10-18) Free forever for up to 10 workspace members, with 1,000 AI credits a month by the pricing page and 200MB of storage (a new account we tested on 21 October 2026, with no subscription, showed 5,000 of 5,000 AI credits included, resetting a month later, and a default AI spending limit of $500 a day; whether the extra credits are a one-off starting allowance is not established); Starter $5 per user a month and Teams $12 per user a month on yearly billing, which the page states saves 33% against monthly; Enterprise is custom. Read the Starter row before you pay for it: it lifts storage to unlimited and AI credits to 3,000 a month, but it keeps the same 10-member cap as Free and adds a 10-project cap. Only Teams, at $12 with 5,000 AI credits, gives unlimited workspace members. The add-ons are the part to budget: proofing and approvals, timesheets, team resourcing, advanced dashboards, SSO and enterprise controls, and external users each cost $5 per user a month on top, which their own calculator confirms. Two further add-ons, CRM and Finance, are listed on the page with no price at all. The external-user add-on includes 5 external licences per seat.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 21 October 2026 on a new account without a subscription: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We made a private project with three dated tasks, assigned them, completed one, opened the Gantt view and read the AI usage and billing screens.
findings: Onboarding runs in five steps. At the invite step, 'Allow users with @aibuildermarketplace.com domain to join the workspace automatically' was ticked by default; we switched it off. The workspace then opened with five sample projects and three demo colleagues.
A blank project can be made 'Private to me'; the default is 'Everyone'. All six layouts (List, Status, Team, Calendar, Gantt, Table) were offered without a lock.
Typing a name and pressing Enter created three tasks in quick succession; due dates of 22, 23 and 24 October set with the date picker stayed correct.
Ticking off one task removed it from the List view (the count went from 3 to 2), because a default filter hides completed actions. A buyer who does not know this will think the task is gone.
The Gantt view worked without a paywall and placed the three tasks on 22, 23 and 24 October.

AI usage showed 5,000 of 5,000 credits remaining (5,000 included, 0 purchased, resetting on 21 November), while the pricing page gives Free '1,000 AI credits / month'. Billing showed a default daily limit, 'Pause AI after $500 per day', with auto top-up off until a card is added.
not_tested: Task descriptions and My Actions on the Home page
Buzz and the other AI features, mail, forms and time tracking
Whether the 5,000 AI credits come back every month or are a one-off starting allowance
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
